domain: Constitutional Law / Political Systems / Comparative Government
topic_summary: Analysis of competing interpretations of the French Fifth Republic Constitution as a commitment system kernel. Two fundamentally incompatible readings exist: a hyper-presidential reading granting near-unmediated sovereign executive power, versus a parliamentary-constrained reading requiring legislative coordination. Both readings claim fidelity to the same constitutional text, but instantiate structurally different constraints on democratic governance.

key_entities: Constitution of the Fifth Republic (founding text, 1958)
President of the Republic (executive office with contested scope)
National Assembly (legislative body with contested constraint power)
key_tensions: Executive sovereignty vs legislative constraint (competing readings of Articles 5, 15, 16, 49.3)
Plebiscitary legitimacy vs parliamentary legitimacy (dual authority sources in same document)
key_mechanisms: Article 16 emergency powers (presidential suspension of normal constraints)
Article 49.3 confidence vote bypass (legislative constraint override)
Cohabitation periods (forced parliamentary reading when president lacks Assembly majority)
key_absences: Explicit hierarchy between presidential and parliamentary authority sources when they conflict

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The 1958 Constitution as stabilized commitment defining legitimate executive authority scope and legislative constraint power
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Constitutional Council formally interprets; presidents and prime ministers claim competing readings in practice; original framers (de Gaulle/Debré) invoked as interpretive anchors

readings.commitment: President as direct sovereign embodying national will, minimally constrained by legislature
readings.authority_grounding: Plebiscitary legitimacy via direct election (1962 reform); Gaullist founding intent; Articles 5, 15, 16 as grant of sovereign decision-making
readings.expected_structural_delta: Legislature enters victim set when president invokes Article 49.3 or Article 16; executive extractiveness high; democratic constraint weak; beneficiary is presidency as institution and incumbent president

readings.commitment: President as coordinated executive requiring legislative authorization for policy implementation
readings.authority_grounding: Parliamentary sovereignty tradition; Articles 20-21 (government responsible to Assembly); constitutional practice during cohabitation periods
readings.expected_structural_delta: Executive enters victim set when Assembly withholds confidence or blocks legislation; executive extractiveness low; democratic constraint strong; beneficiary is legislative majority

readings.commitment: Dual executive requiring negotiated authority allocation between president and prime minister
readings.authority_grounding: Constitutional practice 1986-1988, 1993-1995, 1997-2002; Article 8 (president appoints PM acceptable to Assembly); pragmatic resolution of ambiguity
readings.expected_structural_delta: Both president and Assembly constrain each other; extractiveness moderate but unstable; beneficiary is whichever actor controls key policy domains (foreign vs domestic split); victim is policy coherence

axiom_contradictions.basis: No single constitutional framework can hold both 'president as sovereign minimally constrained' and 'president as executive requiring legislative authorization' simultaneously. Accepting one axiom requires rejecting the other's foundational claim about where legitimate authority resides.

axes.structural_delta: President as direct sovereign embodying national will with minimal legislative constraint
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of Article 49.3 invocations, Article 16 usage, presidential decree authority exercised without legislative pre-approval
axes.selection_reason: Core reading instantiating high extractiveness; axiom-contradictory with parliamentary reading

axes.structural_delta: President as coordinated executive requiring legislative authorization
axes.primary_observable: Government formation requiring Assembly confidence, legislative veto frequency, cohabitation period duration
axes.selection_reason: Axiom-contradictory alternative reading; structurally opposite epsilon and beneficiary/victim structure

axes.structural_delta: Negotiated authority allocation between president and Assembly-backed prime minister
axes.primary_observable: Policy domain split (foreign/defense vs domestic), duration of cohabitation periods, frequency of inter-executive conflicts
axes.selection_reason: Third live reading demonstrating licensed plurality; documents how contradictory readings coexist in practice

axes.structural_delta: Constitutional mechanism allowing president to suspend normal constraints during crisis
axes.primary_observable: Article 16 invocation frequency, duration, scope of measures taken
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: extreme extractiveness but captured as special case within hyper-presidential reading

axes.structural_delta: Ex-ante constitutional review mechanism limiting both presidential and legislative action
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of Council invalidations of government acts, scope of review
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: affects both readings but not itself a reading of the executive authority kernel

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Constitutional crisis mechanism suspending normal constraints
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Extreme but rare case captured within hyper-presidential reading; historical invocation data limited

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Judicial review constraining both executive and legislature
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Cross-cutting constraint affecting both readings but not itself a reading of executive authority kernel

omegas.description: Does cohabitation equilibrium reading genuinely instantiate a third constraint, or does it collapse into parliamentary reading when tested? Cohabitation forces negotiation but may not establish stable third framework.
omegas.source: §1.3-K coherence test; structural delta appears distinct but may be situational rather than foundational

omegas.description: Did the 2000 quinquennat reform (aligning presidential and legislative terms) structurally eliminate cohabitation possibility, thereby collapsing three-reading kernel into de facto binary hyper-presidential vs parliamentary contest?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory); mechanism change may have altered kernel structure

omegas.description: Is Gaullist original intent legitimate interpretive authority, or does constitutional evolution since 1958 supersede framers' reading? If superseded, hyper-presidential reading loses primary authority grounding.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan); founding intent invocation benefits presidency institutionally

omegas.description: Can axiom-contradictory readings coexist indefinitely via domain split and cohabitation practice, or does the contradiction require eventual resolution? If resolution required, which reading survives depends on future electoral outcomes.
omegas.source: §1.3-K axiom contradiction declaration; licensed plurality may be stable or transitional

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition yields three structurally distinct readings with different epsilon values, beneficiary/victim structures, and authority groundings. Axiom contradiction properly declared between hyper-presidential and parliamentary readings. Cohabitation reading documented as pragmatic resolution demonstrating licensed plurality.
